proposed_from.topic:
Ordinary new-topic generation after the mandated revival_remaining.sh count printed zero. This is not a revival of the rejected known-generator commutator: the target is a sharp partially identified continuous-time component risk when only grouped factual event laws are observed. Retain the exact active-ceiling finite-piece theorem over every compatible measurable hazard model; inactive-ceiling pulse bounds, interval existence, mesh rates and generic confidence inversion cannot substitute for it. MODEL: Fixed known T>0,L>0, arbitrary finite fixed grid 0=t0<...<tK=T. iid subjects, A randomized Bernoulli(1/2), no covariates or additional censoring. Absorbing first-event system: four deterministic Lebesgue-measurable cause-specific hazards lambda_j^a:[0,T]->[0,L], a in {0,1}, j in {1,2}. Under component intervention (aY,aD), cause1 hazard is lambda1^aY and cause2 hazard lambda2^aD; survival is exp(-integral(lambda1^aY+lambda2^aD)). This hazard-splicing restriction defines the causal model; no latent independence beyond what realizes these intervention laws is asserted. All such quadruples are allowed. Observe only A and first-failure inspection bin plus adjudicated cause, or survival to T; retain neither exact failure time nor within-bin order. The population observation is factual conditional bin triples z_ak=(p_ak,q_ak,s_ak), summing to1. Survival is positive because hazards are bounded. Restrict z to compatible observations. Target psi=integral_0^T exp(-Lambda1^1(t)-Lambda2^0(t)) lambda1^1(t)dt, and SDE=psi-observed arm0 cause1 risk. No sensitivity analysis: the hazard-component model is maintained and coarsening produces partial identification. KERNEL: Conjecture over every L,T,K,grid and compatible z: derive a sharp constructive representation of the full attainable hybrid incidence-survival frontier for ONE bin, sufficient to evaluate its support envelope H_z(v)=sup(r+v*s) and lower envelope h_z(v)=inf(r+v*s), for v in [0,1]. Here (r,s) is the hybrid cause1 incidence and end-survival within that bin, generated by four bounded hazards reproducing both factual triples. These suprema define the object, NOT the promised solution. The hard assertion is that exact envelopes admit a uniformly finite switching representation: there exists a universal finite integer B, independent of z,L,bin width, such that each envelope value is attained by compatible piecewise-constant hazard quadruples with at most B common subintervals; levels may be anywhere in [0,L], not necessarily bang-bang. Derive an explicit valid B and finite parameter optimization with endpoint probability constraints and objective expressed in elementary exponential integrals; characterize the optimizing incidence-survival tradeoff beyond merely invoking general optimal control. Prove global endpoints by backward evaluation U_(K+1)=D_(K+1)=0, U_k=H_zk(U_(k+1)), D_k=h_zk(D_(k+1)), including compatible full-model gluing. Also derive the worst-case identification-width order over compatible z: for each fixed M>0 and LT<=M, sufficiently small L*max(bin width), sup_z(U1-D1) is bounded above and below by positive constants depending only on M times L^2*sum(bin width^2). Constants and the finite-switch bound B are delegated derivation objects; the finite-switch EXISTENCE and matched mesh order are conjectures, not established claims. Sampling rung: invert an explicit simultaneous multinomial confidence region through the endpoint computation to obtain an interval containing the entire population identified set with coverage at least1-alpha uniformly over the class; report computational approximation error separately if used. No one-bin result or generic discretization substitutes for the hard finite-switch frontier theorem. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derives exact factual-bin compatibility, compactness and interval sharpness in survival-flow coordinates, an exact active-ceiling frontier with one saturated factual arm, and compatible global gluing. For two positive factual triples with survival exp(-1.6), an exact five-piece family has a quartic restricted support optimizer: at continuation zero its hybrid risk is 0.47070698750422113 with survival 0.18947781529999005. Root independently checked the path probabilities; global optimality is not established. Switching equations make two nuisance controls monotone; a proposed simultaneous logistic singular obstruction fails the Goh necessary condition, while single-control singular arcs admit exact pulse replacement. Matched mesh-width bounds and multinomial inversion coverage are derived supporting results. Fixed-grid optimizations supply feasible values only, and current primary checks found no direct solved collision.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove parameter-uniform endpoint-preserving compression of optimal alternating bang trajectories when both nuisance hazards are saturated and factual-incidence multipliers are negative; assemble all flat, singular, abnormal and boundary cases into an explicit universal finite B.
EARLY KILL TEST: Parameterize two full four-corner cycles, compute factual constraints and support objective exactly, and examine the constrained Hessian for an improving cycle-deletion direction or an optimality-certified obstruction. Do not replace the finite-piece theorem with mesh bounds or numerical gridding.

proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest causal results identify the same hybrid risk when exact or temporally ordered hazards are recoverable; the closest econometric bounds solve a different latent-duration model; and the closest control results guarantee only relaxed or asymptotic optimization and explicitly allow chattering. The common numerical ceiling is therefore disclosed as a novel maintained sensitivity-model restriction calibrated from external exact-time or audited-intensity information, not misclassified as standard separable-effects regularity; identified sets are required to nest when the ceiling is conservatively enlarged. Conditional on that transparent model, the proposed field-level advance is an exact, parameter-uniform finite representation of both active-ceiling one-bin support envelopes while preserving two factual incidence constraints, two factual survival constraints, the hybrid objective, and chronological exponential survival. The fully specified positive-cell two-cycle Hessian and pulse-exchange predicate exposes the shortest falsification route. The recursion, sensitivity corollary, mesh modulus, and confidence inversion are consumers and supporting results rather than substitutes for the kernel.

anchor.opened_evidence: The source establishes the resolved-time cross-arm hazard integral and derives its influence-function representation; its proof begins with known cause-specific cumulative hazards.

seed_details.theorem_kernel: For every compatible one-bin grouped law and continuation value, determine whether both sharp support extrema admit an exact universal finite common-piece hazard representation; derive an explicit bound and finite exponential program, or construct a family forcing unbounded switching.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The resolved-time hazard integral can no longer be evaluated because grouping identifies only factual endpoint flows; the first replacement is optimization over all bounded hazard paths satisfying four factual endpoint constraints.
seed_details.destination_search: Focused searches for grouped or interval-censored separable effects, hazard-spliced sharp bounds, and bounded-hazard switching found resolved-time estimators and discrete latent-duration bounds but no solved frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from occupation-measure atomicity because only finitely many endpoint moments are constrained.
seed_details.rebuttal: Atomic occupation measures discard chronological state evolution; exponentiated survival and cross-arm splicing depend on ordered cumulative hazards, while generic smooth control problems can chatter.

seed_details.theorem_kernel: Prove a uniform two-sided law for worst-compatible separable-risk width of order L² times the sum of squared bin widths, with positive-cell lower witnesses and survival propagation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the paper's qualitative fine-grid argument by a second-order comparison of all within-bin rearrangements having the same factual probabilities, followed by exact backward accumulation.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining inspection mesh, separable effects, grouped competing risks, and identification modulus returned statistical current-status rates but no deterministic causal-width modulus.
seed_details.red_team: A Taylor expansion of the continuous-time g-formula gives the rate immediately.
seed_details.rebuttal: The upper bound must be uniform over merely measurable adversarial hazards, while the matching lower bound must preserve factual compatibility and accumulate through the exact nonlinear recursion.

seed_details.theorem_kernel: Characterize the tangential Hadamard directional derivative of the recursively composed sharp endpoint map when compatibility constraints move with grouped probabilities and optimizers tie or change switching regime.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Danskin differentiation must be replaced by sensitivity analysis for a probability-dependent nonconvex feasible set, including active compatibility constraints and composition across bins.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for directional derivatives of grouped competing-risk sharp bounds with moving feasibility constraints found general value-function inference and directional delta methods, but not this endpoint map.
seed_details.red_team: A standard Danskin theorem and chain rule already give the derivative.
seed_details.rebuttal: Standard Danskin formulas hold for a fixed feasible set; here the probability vector changes the endpoint equalities and can alter feasibility dimension at compatibility boundaries.

anchor.opened_evidence: The paper supplies the exact nonlinear state functional that becomes the grouped-data control objective.

seed_details.theorem_kernel: Construct an occupation-measure relaxation for the one-bin frontier and characterize observable conditions under which a finite relaxation is exact and recovers an ordinary bounded-hazard optimizer.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Lift the coupled factual and hybrid survival ODE to occupation measures while retaining endpoint incidence equalities, then prove a no-relaxation-gap recovery criterion rather than asymptotic hierarchy convergence alone.
seed_details.destination_search: The target–method search found Lasserre-type convergent moment hierarchies but no finite-convergence or ordinary-control recovery theorem for hazard-spliced incidence constraints.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine application of polynomial optimal-control relaxations.
seed_details.rebuttal: Routine relaxations provide bounds converging with degree; the proposed kernel requires an exact finite certificate and recovery of an ordered ordinary control, which those theorems do not supply.
seed_details.outcome: dropped-after-deepening because it risks replacing the required exact finite-piece theorem with relaxation theory

seed_details.theorem_kernel: Partition the compatible one-bin probability region into ceiling-activity regimes and derive closed-form sharp incidence-survival envelopes on every regime boundary and full-dimensional cell where a fixed pulse ordering is globally optimal.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The sequential g-formula substitution is replaced by a global rearrangement comparison among bounded continuous-time hazard orders that reproduce the same factual triples.

seed_details.red_team: The result is only a case-by-case rearrangement exercise once the hazard ceiling is imposed.

seed_details.theorem_kernel: Project an exact simultaneous two-arm multinomial confidence region through globally certified sharp endpoint programs, with empty-intersection fallback and deterministic outward accounting for numerical error.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After the source's input-law coverage event is established, replace ordinary parameter inclusion by set-valued projection through compatibility-restricted nonconvex lower and upper endpoint maps.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found exact multinomial regions and inference for scalar multinomial functionals, but not coverage of an entire optimized causal identified set with certified global-program error.
seed_details.red_team: Coverage follows immediately from confidence-region projection.
seed_details.rebuttal: The probability argument is short, but practical validity additionally requires exact compatibility handling and one-sided certificates for both nested nonconvex optimizations; nevertheless this remains a supporting rather than headline contribution.
seed_details.outcome: dropped as standalone kernel; retained as supporting theorem

anchor.opened_evidence: The SPRINT analysis uses scheduled monthly or quarterly measurements, while the theory offers no quantitative rule for choosing inspection times.

seed_details.theorem_kernel: Under a known time-varying hazard ceiling, characterize the fixed K-bin inspection grid minimizing worst-compatible component-risk ambiguity and certify its minimax value.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Generalize the local second-order ambiguity from L²Δ² to a ceiling-weighted bin functional, then optimize the globally propagated modulus over ordered inspection times.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for optimal inspection design for separable effects or partial-identification width found likelihood-based visit scheduling but no minimax causal-ambiguity design.
seed_details.red_team: Equal-width bins are immediate from convexity of the mesh bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: With heterogeneous ceilings and survival propagation the local costs are unequal and endogenous to prior exposure; the exact minimax grid need not be uniform.
seed_details.outcome: dropped because it changes the fixed-common-ceiling model before the base frontier is solved

seed_details.theorem_kernel: Develop an output-sensitive exact inversion algorithm whose complexity depends on active compatible switching patterns rather than all multinomial cells, while retaining finite-sample identified-set coverage at sparse laws.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace pointwise membership checks in the likelihood-level-set region by branch-and-bound over compatibility cells coupled to certified endpoint envelopes.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for sparse exact multinomial inversion combined with nonconvex partial-identification maps found no direct method.
seed_details.red_team: This is computational engineering around an existing coverage theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: A theorem giving provable complexity and outward endpoint certificates would be substantive, but its value depends on first resolving finite switching.
seed_details.outcome: dropped because it is downstream of the unresolved structural kernel

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected finite-switch seed was deepened against four adjacent threads. Stensrud, Young, Didelez, Robins, and Hernán (JASA 2022, Sections 5–6 and Supplementary Appendix B) identify separable risks under treatment decomposition but fix discrete within-period order. Martinussen and Stensrud (Biometrics 2023, Sections 2.3–2.4 and Appendix 8.1) derive the resolved-time cross-arm hazard integral and influence function, requiring event-time hazard inputs unavailable from grouped triples. Kim (Journal of Econometrics 2023, Sections 2–4, cross-checked against the public thesis chapter) obtains sequential nonlinear bounds for discretely measured latent competing durations, not bounded-hazard component interventions. Lasserre, Henrion, Prieur, and Trélat (SIAM JCO 2008, Theorems 2.3 and 3.6 with proofs) provide occupation-measure and moment-relaxation bounds, but neither finite convergence nor recovery by a universal number of ordered ordinary-control pieces. Zhu, Trélat, and Cerf (DCDS-B 2016) supplies the adverse chattering comparator showing why Pontryagin conditions are insufficient. Bayer and Teichmann (Proceedings AMS 2006) supplies finite atomic moment compression but does not preserve chronological survival dynamics. A current search also checked Park and Suk's 2026 two-arm/four-arm separable-effects preprint; its target is identification, estimation, and falsification across component-assignment designs, not grouped hazard frontiers. For the mesh seed, Stensrud et al. (Lifetime Data Analysis 2021), Schmid and Berger (WIREs 2021), Groeneboom, Maathuis, and Wellner (Annals 2008), and Maathuis and Hudgens (Biometrika 2011) confirm that existing fine-grid discussion is qualitative or concerns factual sampling rates. For the derivative seed, Fang and Santos (ReStud 2019) and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (JoE 2023) provide directional-delta and optimized-value machinery but do not treat probability-dependent feasibility. No closer paper located in the focused target–method searches subsumes the selected kernel.
